premise: When my father died, his will left me a $265,000 collection of Depression‑era glass, but my sister—the executor—forged a $1 sale note and sold it to a museum for $300,000; I forced open the museum’s provenance records, proved the forgery, recovered the entire collection, and opened ‘Shattered Trust Glass Studio’ where she is court‑ordered to polish each piece wearing white gloves printed with ‘Fraud Fragile’ while visitors receive a postcard with her perjury conviction.
